Home Widgets Docs

HTML is the application.
JavaScript just does what it's told.

Alpine and htmx brought logic closer to HTML. Popstart inverts it completely — your markup is the app, functions are just plumbing. No virtual DOM, no shadow DOM, no JSX, no build step. Chain functions from attributes, swap components with selectors, theme everything with CSS variables. 194 widgets. 57KB raw / 18KB gzipped. One script tag.

<button ps-click="validate, save, __.alertSuccess" save-url="/api/data" alertSuccess-msg="Saved!">Submit</button>

See it in action

Every interaction below is wired through ps-* attributes — the same pattern for tabs, modals, forms, drag-and-drop, and 190 more components.

Tab Panels zero JS

__.switchTo · one attribute per tab

Event binding, function chains, DOM helpers, HTTP wrappers, form scraping, templating, streaming, cookies, storage — all from HTML attributes.

No virtual DOM diffing. No reconciliation. Direct DOM access means updates happen in microseconds, not milliseconds.

Core + extras is ~57KB unminified (~18KB gzipped). Smaller than jQuery minified (87KB). Plugins lazy-load on demand.

HTML
<!-- Counter: zero custom JavaScript -->
<div class="counter-display" id="count">0</div>
<div class="counter-btns">
  <button ps-click="stepVal"
    stepVal-selector="#count"
    stepVal-step="-1"
    debounce="0">&#8722; Decrement</button>
  <button ps-click="stepVal"
    stepVal-selector="#count"
    stepVal-step="1"
    debounce="0">+ Increment</button>
</div>
JavaScript
// stepVal is a reusable helper included in Popstart:
function stepVal(selector, step, min, max) {
  var el = document.querySelector(selector)
  if (!el) return
  var v = parseFloat(el.textContent) || 0
  v += parseFloat(step) || 0
  if (min !== undefined && min !== '') v = Math.max(v, parseFloat(min))
  if (max !== undefined && max !== '') v = Math.min(v, parseFloat(max))
  el.textContent = v
}
// Optional: add stepVal-min="0" stepVal-max="99" to clamp values

  __.text('#output', 'ERROR: ' + msg)

Tabs & Panels

Tab Panels zero JS

__.switchTo · one-line tab switching

Popstart maps HTML attributes to JavaScript functions. Events become declarations.

<script src="popstart-core.js"></script>
No npm, no webpack. One script tag.

Write a function. Name it in an attribute. Popstart calls it when the event fires.

Scroll Spy

IntersectionObserver · scroll-linked nav highlighting
Introduction

Popstart maps DOM events directly to JavaScript functions via HTML attributes. No virtual DOM, no build step, no framework overhead. Every interaction is declared in markup and executed by a tiny runtime.

The library watches the DOM for elements with ps-* attributes and binds the specified events automatically. When the DOM changes, bindings update.

Installation

Add a single <script> tag. No npm, no webpack, no bundler configuration. Works with any backend or static site.

The full build is ~18KB gzipped. A tiny build (core only) is under 6KB. Load from CDN or self-host — no dependencies.

Configuration

Customize event bindings, debounce timing, attribute prefixes, and logging levels through __.config. Defaults work for most apps.

Override __.config.AttributePrefix to use data-ps-* instead of ps-* for strict HTML validation.

API Reference

Built-in functions: __.show, __.hide, __.toggle, __.switchTo, __.css, __.addClass, __.removeClass, __.toggleClass, and many more.

Every function works with CSS selectors. Chain them in attributes: ps-click="validate, save, __.alertSuccess".

Scroll the content panel — the nav highlights the section currently in view. Click a nav item to jump.

HTML
<div class="scrollspy-layout" id="my-spy">
  <nav class="scrollspy-nav">
    <button class="spy-link active"
      data-spy-target="#section-1">Intro</button>
    <button class="spy-link" data-spy-target="#section-2">Install</button>
  </nav>
  <div class="scrollspy-content" id="spy-scroll">
    <div class="scrollspy-section" id="section-1">...</div>
    <div class="scrollspy-section" id="section-2">...</div>
  </div>
</div>
JavaScript
// Nav click → scroll within container (not the page)
document.querySelectorAll('.scrollspy-layout').forEach(widget => {
  if (widget.dataset.spyInit) return
  widget.dataset.spyInit = '1'
  var scroll = widget.querySelector('.scrollspy-content')
  var links = widget.querySelectorAll('.spy-link')
  var sections = widget.querySelectorAll('.scrollspy-section')
  links.forEach(btn => {
    btn.onclick = () => {
      var t = widget.querySelector(btn.dataset.spyTarget)
      if (!t) return
      scroll.scrollTo({top: t.offsetTop - scroll.offsetTop, behavior:'smooth'})
    }
  })
  var observer = new IntersectionObserver(entries => {
    entries.forEach(e => {
      if (!e.isIntersecting) return
      links.forEach(b =>
        b.classList.toggle('active', b.dataset.spyTarget === '#'+e.target.id))
    })
  }, {root: scroll, threshold: 0.4})
  sections.forEach(s => observer.observe(s))
})

Table of Contents zero JS

__.scrollTo · mini TOC with smooth scroll

1. Getting Started

Include Popstart with a single script tag. No build tools needed. Your HTML attributes become event bindings instantly.

2. Configuration

Customize event names, debounce intervals, and attribute prefixes through the __.config object. Override defaults per element with attributes.

3. Event Binding

Popstart listens for click, mouseup, change, input, keyup, and submit events. Add more via __.config.BoundEventNames array.

4. Function Chaining

Comma-separated function names in an attribute create a sequential promise chain. Each function completes before the next begins.

5. Advanced Topics

Data paths, error handlers, suffix patterns, and DOM watching enable complex interactions without leaving HTML.

Modal Dialog

This uses __.show to open and __.hide to close. Backdrop click dismisses. Inner __.noop stops propagation. Zero custom JS.

CSS
/* Utility class to hide elements */
.hidden { display: none !important; }

/* Fullscreen backdrop -- click anywhere to dismiss */
.modal-bg {
  position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 200;
  background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);
  backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  animation: fadeIn .2s;
}

/* Centered dialog box */
.modal-box {
  background: var(--card, #1c2028);
  border: 1px solid var(--card-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.08));
  border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 2rem;
  max-width: 420px;
  width: 90%;
  box-shadow: 0 20px 60px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4);
  animation: modalIn .25s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
}
.modal-box h3 { margin-bottom: 0.75rem; }
.modal-box p  {
  font-size: 15px;
  color: var(--fg2, #9a9590);
  margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
  line-height: 1.7;
}

@keyframes fadeIn {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(4px); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
}
@keyframes modalIn {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-20px) scale(0.95); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
}

  ps-click="__.hide" hide-selector="#my-modal"

  <!-- __.noop stops click from bubbling to backdrop -->

    <h3>Modal Dialog</h3>

      with <code>__.noop</code>. Zero custom JavaScript.</p>

  </div>
</div>

// zero custom JavaScript needed
// __.show  removes .hidden from the backdrop  -- modal appears
// __.hide  adds .hidden back                  -- modal disappears
// __.noop  on inner box stops click propagation to backdrop

      alertInfo-msg="Copied"

JavaScript
function showContextMenu(e) {
  e.preventDefault();
  var menu = document.getElementById('ctx-menu-panel');
  var area = e.currentTarget;
  var rect = area.getBoundingClientRect();
  menu.style.left = (e.clientX - rect.left) + 'px';
  menu.style.top = (e.clientY - rect.top) + 'px';
  menu.classList.remove('hidden');
  // dismiss on next click anywhere
  document.addEventListener('click', function dismiss() {
    menu.classList.add('hidden');
    document.removeEventListener('click', dismiss);
  }, { once: true });
}

JavaScript
// Bind per widget instance, not by page-global id
let container = document.querySelector('.imgzoom-container')
let box = container.querySelector('.imgzoom-surface')
let lens = container.querySelector('.imgzoom-lens')
box.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {
  let rect = box.getBoundingClientRect()
  let x = e.clientX - rect.left, y = e.clientY - rect.top
  lens.style.left = (x - 40) + 'px'
  lens.style.top = (y - 40) + 'px'
  lens.style.display = 'block'
})
box.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => lens.style.display = 'none')

    HTML
    <!-- Form: __.scrape reads input values into __.data, then addTodo runs -->
<form ps-submit="__.scrape, addTodo"
  style="display:flex;gap:0.5rem">
  <input type="text" name="task" placeholder="Add a task..." required style="flex:1">
  <button type="submit">Add</button>
</form>

<!-- Todo items are appended here by renderTodos() -->
<ul class="todo-list" id="todo-list"></ul>
    JavaScript
    function addTodo(el) {
  var task = ((__.data.form && __.data.form.task) || '').trim()
  if (!task) return
  var todos = __.store('ps-todos') || []
  todos.push(task)
  __.store('ps-todos', todos)
  renderTodos()
  __.el('input[name=task]', el)[0].value = ''
}

function renderTodos() {
  var ul = document.getElementById('todo-list')
  if (!ul) return
  ul.textContent = ''
  var todos = __.store('ps-todos') || []
  todos.forEach(function(task, i) {
    __.append('#todo-list',
      '&lt;li&gt;&lt;span&gt;' + task +
      '&lt;/span&gt;&lt;button class="del-btn" ' +
      'ps-click="removeTodo" removeTodo-idx="' + i +
      '"&gt;&amp;times;&lt;/button&gt;&lt;/li&gt;')
  })
  __.Popstart()   // rebind events on new elements
}

function removeTodo(idx) {
  var todos = __.store('ps-todos') || []
  todos.splice(Number(idx), 1)
  __.store('ps-todos', todos)
  renderTodos()
}

// restore saved todos on page load
renderTodos()

    CSS
    /* Toggle track -- the pill-shaped background */
.toggle-track {
  width: 48px;
  height: 26px;
  border-radius: 13px;
  background: var(--card-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.08));
  cursor: pointer;
  position: relative;
  display: inline-block;
  vertical-align: middle;
  transition: background 0.2s;
}

/* The sliding knob (pure CSS, no extra element) */
.toggle-track::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  top: 3px;
  left: 3px;
  width: 20px;
  height: 20px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--contrast, #fff);
  transition: transform 0.2s;
}

/* "on" state -- accent background + knob slides right */
.toggle-track.on {
  background: var(--accent, #e08a4a);
}
.toggle-track.on::after {
  transform: translateX(22px);
}

    Password Strength

    ps-input · __.css · strength scoring
    Type to check strength

<div class="strength-track">
  <div class="strength-bar" id="str-bar"></div>
</div>
    JavaScript
    function checkStrength(el) {
  let p = el.value, score = 0
  if (p.length > 5) score++
  if (p.length > 10) score++
  if (/[a-z]/.test(p) && /[A-Z]/.test(p)) score++
  if (/\d/.test(p)) score++
  if (/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/.test(p)) score++
  let pct = Math.min(score * 20, 100)
  let color = pct < 40 ? 'var(--error)'
            : pct < 70 ? 'var(--warning)'
            : 'var(--success)'
  __.css('#str-bar', 'width', pct + '%')
  __.css('#str-bar', 'background', color)
}

    JavaScript
    function inlineEditStart(displaysel, inputsel, inputel) {
  __.hide(displaysel)
  __.show(inputsel)
  document.querySelector(inputel).focus()
}

function inlineEditSave(ev, displaysel, inputsel, textsel, inputel) {
  if (ev.key === 'Escape') {
    document.querySelector(inputel).value =
      document.querySelector(textsel).textContent
    __.hide(inputsel); __.show(displaysel)
  }
  if (ev.key === 'Enter') {
    __.text(textsel, document.querySelector(inputel).value)
    __.hide(inputsel); __.show(displaysel)
  }
}

function inlineEditBlur(displaysel, inputsel, textsel, inputel) {
  __.text(textsel, document.querySelector(inputel).value)
  __.hide(inputsel); __.show(displaysel)
}

    PIN Input

    Popstart-driven · ps-input · auto-advance · turns green on fill
    Enter your 6-digit code
    HTML
    <div class="pin-wrap" id="pin-container">
  <input type="text" class="pin-box" maxlength="1" data-pin="0"
    ps-input="pinAdvance"
    pinAdvance-container="#pin-container"
    pinAdvance-status="#pin-status"
    ps-keyup="pinKeyNav"
    pinKeyNav-container="#pin-container" />
  <!-- repeat for each digit... -->
</div>
<div id="pin-status">Enter your 6-digit code</div>
    JavaScript
    function pinAdvance(el, container, status) {
  var boxes = document.querySelectorAll(container + ' .pin-box')
  var idx = Number(el.dataset.pin)
  if (el.value.length === 1) {
    el.classList.add('filled')
    if (idx < boxes.length - 1) boxes[idx + 1].focus()
  }
  // Check if all filled
  var code = ''
  boxes.forEach(function(b) { code += b.value })
  if (code.length === boxes.length) {
    __.text(status, 'Code entered: ' + code)
  } else {
    __.text(status, 'Enter your 6-digit code')
  }
}

function pinKeyNav(ev, el, container) {
  var boxes = document.querySelectorAll(container + ' .pin-box')
  var idx = Number(el.dataset.pin)
  if (ev.key === 'Backspace' && !el.value && idx > 0) {
    boxes[idx - 1].focus()
    boxes[idx - 1].value = ''
    boxes[idx - 1].classList.remove('filled')
  }
}

    JavaScript
    // drag events are not in Popstart's bound set
// requires a small JS setup:
const dz = document.getElementById('dropzone-area')
dz.addEventListener('click', () =>
  document.getElementById('dropzone-input').click())
dz.addEventListener('dragover', e => {
  e.preventDefault(); dz.classList.add('dragover') })
dz.addEventListener('dragleave', () =>
  dz.classList.remove('dragover'))
dz.addEventListener('drop', e => {
  e.preventDefault(); dz.classList.remove('dragover')
  showFiles(e.dataTransfer.files) })
document.getElementById('dropzone-input')
  .addEventListener('change', e => showFiles(e.target.files))
function showFiles(files) {
  document.getElementById('dropzone-files').textContent =
    [...files].map(f => f.name).join(', ')
}

    // auto-focus requires JS (keyup auto-advance)
document.querySelectorAll('.otp-digit').forEach(inp => {
  inp.addEventListener('input', e => {
    const v = e.target.value.replace(/\D/g,'')
    e.target.value = v
    if (v && e.target.nextElementSibling)
      e.target.nextElementSibling.focus()
    checkOtp()
  })
  inp.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
    if (e.key==='Backspace' && !e.target.value
        && e.target.previousElementSibling)
      e.target.previousElementSibling.focus()
  })
})
function checkOtp() {
  const digits = [...document.querySelectorAll('.otp-digit')]
    .map(i => i.value).join('')
  if (digits.length === 6)
    document.getElementById('otp-status')
      .textContent = '\u2713 Code entered: ' + digits
}

    function tlToggle() {
  this.classList.toggle('selected')
  this.querySelector('input').checked =
    this.classList.contains('selected')
}
function tlMove(dir) {
  let src = dir==='right' ? '#tl-left' : '#tl-right'
  let dst = dir==='right' ? '#tl-right' : '#tl-left'
  document.querySelectorAll(src+' .selected')
    .forEach(el => {
      el.classList.remove('selected')
      el.querySelector('input').checked = false
      document.querySelector(dst).appendChild(el)
    })
  __.Popstart()
}

    JavaScript
    let tpH=9, tpM=30, tpP='AM'
// Parse "2:30pm", "14:30", "2:30 PM" formats
function tpParseTime(str) {
  str = str.trim().toLowerCase()
  var m = str.match(/^(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*(am|pm)?$/)
  if (!m) return null
  var h=parseInt(m[1]), min=parseInt(m[2]),
      period=m[3]
  if (min<0||min>59) return null
  if (!period && h>=0 && h<=23) {
    period = h>=12 ? 'pm' : 'am'
    if (h>12) h-=12; if (h===0) h=12
  }
  if (h<1||h>12) return null
  return {h:h, m:min, p:period.toUpperCase()}
}
function tpQuick(h, m, p) {
  if (p==='now') {
    var d=new Date(); var hr=d.getHours()
    tpP=hr>=12?'PM':'AM'
    tpH=hr%12||12; tpM=d.getMinutes()
  } else { tpH=+h; tpM=+m; tpP=p }
  tpRender()
}
function tpSetFromInput() {
  var r = tpParseTime(
    document.getElementById('tp-text-input').value)
  if (r) { tpH=r.h; tpM=r.m; tpP=r.p; tpRender() }
}

    ps-input · auto-formatting phone & credit card

    JavaScript
    function maskPhone() {
  let d = this.value.replace(/\D/g,'').slice(0,10)
  let f = ''
  if (d.length>0) f='('+d.slice(0,3)
  if (d.length>=3) f+=') '+d.slice(3,6)
  if (d.length>=6) f+='-'+d.slice(6)
  this.value = f
}
function maskCard() {
  let d = this.value.replace(/\D/g,'').slice(0,16)
  this.value = d.replace(/(.{4})/g,'$1 ').trim()
}

    JavaScript
    function slMove(dir) {
  let li = this.closest('.sl-item')
  if (dir==='up' && li.previousElementSibling)
    li.parentNode.insertBefore(li, li.previousElementSibling)
  else if (dir==='down' && li.nextElementSibling)
    li.parentNode.insertBefore(li.nextElementSibling, li)
}

    /* 3D perspective wrapper */
.cc-scene {
  perspective: 600px;
  display: flex;
  justify-content: center;
  padding: 0.75rem;
}

/* The card itself */
.cc-card {
  width: 280px;
  height: 170px;
  border-radius: 12px;
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1a1a3e, #2a2a5e, #1a1a3e);
  padding: 1rem;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  justify-content: space-between;
  box-shadow: 0 20px 60px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4);
  position: relative;
  overflow: hidden;
}

/* Decorative glow circle */
.cc-card::before {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  width: 200px; height: 200px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: rgba(224, 138, 74, 0.1);
  top: -60px; right: -60px;
}

/* EMV chip */
.cc-chip {
  width: 36px; height: 26px;
  border-radius: 4px;
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #d4a44a, #c89030);
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
}
.cc-chip::after {
  content: '';
  width: 18px; height: 14px;
  border: 1.5px solid rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);
  border-radius: 2px;
}

/* Card number display */
.cc-number {
  font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
  font-size: 16px;
  color: #e0e0e0;
  letter-spacing: 2px;
}

/* Name + expiry row */
.cc-bottom {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: flex-end;
}
.cc-name {
  font-size: 12px; color: #b0b0b0;
  text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1px;
}
.cc-expiry {
  font-size: 12px; color: #b0b0b0;
  font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
}

/* Form inputs below the card */
.cc-form {
  display: grid;
  gap: 0.5rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 0 0;
}
.cc-form input {
  background: var(--bg3, #1c2028);
  border: 1px solid var(--card-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.08));
  color: var(--fg, #e8e4df);
  padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem;
  border-radius: 6px;
  font-size: 13px;
  font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
  outline: none;
}
.cc-form input:focus {
  border-color: var(--accent, #e08a4a);
}
.cc-form-row {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 0.5rem;
}

    JavaScript
    // Live-update the card number display
// Strips non-digits, pads with bullets, groups by 4
function ccUpdateNum() {
  var v = this.value.replace(/\D/g, '').substring(0, 16)
  var display = v
  while (display.length < 16) display += '\u2022'
  var formatted = display.replace(/(.{4})/g, '$1 ').trim()
  this.closest('[data-widget="creditcard"]')
    .querySelector('.cc-number')
    .textContent = formatted
}

// Live-update the cardholder name
function ccUpdateName() {
  var v = this.value.toUpperCase()
  this.closest('[data-widget="creditcard"]')
    .querySelector('.cc-name')
    .textContent = v || 'YOUR NAME'
}

// Live-update the expiry date
function ccUpdateExp() {
  this.closest('[data-widget="creditcard"]')
    .querySelector('.cc-expiry')
    .textContent = this.value || 'MM/YY'
}

    @Mention Input

    ps-input · user dropdown on @ trigger

    JavaScript
    var miUsers = [
  {name:'Alice',init:'A'},{name:'Bob',init:'B'},
  {name:'Sarah',init:'S'},{name:'James',init:'J'},
  {name:'Anna',init:'A'},{name:'Steve',init:'S'}
]
function miSearch() {
  var v = this.value
  var at = v.lastIndexOf('@')
  var wrap = this.closest('.mi-wrap')
  var drop = wrap.querySelector('.mi-dropdown')
  if (at === -1 || at === v.length - 1) {
    drop.classList.remove('show'); return
  }
  var q = v.substring(at + 1).toLowerCase()
  var hits = miUsers.filter(function(u) {
    return u.name.toLowerCase().startsWith(q)
  })
  if (!hits.length) { drop.classList.remove('show'); return }
  drop.innerHTML = hits.map(function(u) {
    return '<div class="mi-item" ps-click="miPick" ' +
      'miPick-name="' + u.name + '" debounce="0">' +
      '<span class="mi-avatar">' +
      u.init + '</span>' + u.name + '</div>'
  }).join('')
  __.Popstart()
  drop.classList.add('show')
}
function miPick(name, el) {
  var wrap = el.closest('.mi-wrap')
  var field = wrap.querySelector('.mi-input')
  var at = field.value.lastIndexOf('@')
  field.value = field.value.substring(0, at) +
    '@' + name + ' '
  wrap.querySelector('.mi-dropdown')
    .classList.remove('show')
  field.focus()
}

    CSS
    /* Carousel container -- hides overflow */
.carousel {
  overflow: hidden;
  border-radius: var(--radius, 8px);
  position: relative;
}

/* Sliding track -- holds all slides side by side */
.carousel-track {
  display: flex;
  transition: transform .4s ease;
}

/* Each slide fills the full width */
.carousel-slide {
  min-width: 100%;
  padding: 2rem;
  text-align: center;
  font-size: 14px;
}
.carousel-slide:nth-child(1) {
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1a2a1a, #0a1a0a);
  color: var(--success, #4caf50);
}
.carousel-slide:nth-child(2) {
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #2a1a1a, #1a0a0a);
  color: var(--error, #e05252);
}
.carousel-slide:nth-child(3) {
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1a1a2a, #0a0a1a);
  color: var(--info, #5b9bd5);
}

/* Arrow buttons */
.carousel-arrow {
  position: absolute;
  top: 50%;
  transform: translateY(-50%);
  width: 32px;
  height: 32px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  border: 1px solid var(--card-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.08));
  background: var(--overlay, rgba(0,0,0,0.4));
  color: var(--contrast, #fff);
  font-size: 16px;
  cursor: pointer;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  transition: all 0.2s;
  z-index: 2;
}
.carousel-arrow:hover {
  background: var(--accent, #e08a4a);
  border-color: var(--accent, #e08a4a);
}
.carousel-prev { left: 10px; }
.carousel-next { right: 10px; }

/* Dot navigation row */
.carousel-nav {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
  margin-top: 0.75rem;
}

    JavaScript
    // Dot buttons are zero-JS (__.css sets transform from attrs)
// Arrow navigation needs a small helper:
var carouselTotal = 3
__.data.carouselIdx = 0

function carouselNav(dir) {
  __.data.carouselIdx =
    (__.data.carouselIdx + parseInt(dir) + carouselTotal)
    % carouselTotal
  carouselGo(__.data.carouselIdx)
}

function carouselGo(idx) {
  __.data.carouselIdx = idx
  __.css('#carousel-track', 'transform',
    'translateX(-' + (idx * 100) + '%)')
  // sync active dot
  var dots = __.el('#carousel-dots .btn')
  dots.forEach(function(d, i) {
    i === idx
      ? d.classList.add('active')
      : d.classList.remove('active')
  })
}

  <div class="progress-bar" id="progress-bar"></div>

<div style="display:flex;gap:0.5rem;align-items:center">
  <button ps-click="simulateProgress"

    JavaScript
    var _progressTimer = null

function simulateProgress() {
  resetProgress()
  var pct = 0
  return new Promise(function(resolve) {
    var tick = function() {
      pct += Math.random() * 15 + 3
      if (pct >= 100) {
        pct = 100; _progressTimer = null
        __.css('#progress-bar', 'width', '100%')
        __.text('#progress-label', '100%')
        resolve(); return
      }
      __.css('#progress-bar', 'width', pct.toFixed(0) + '%')
      __.text('#progress-label', pct.toFixed(0) + '%')
      _progressTimer = setTimeout(tick, 200 + Math.random() * 300)
    }
    tick()
  })
}

function resetProgress() {
  if (_progressTimer) {
    clearTimeout(_progressTimer)
    _progressTimer = null
  }
  __.css('#progress-bar', 'width', '0%')
  __.text('#progress-label', '0%')
}

    __.data.dtSortDir = {}
function dtSort(el, table, col) {
  col = parseInt(col)
  var dir = __.data.dtSortDir[col] = !(__.data.dtSortDir[col])
  var tbody = document.querySelector(table + ' tbody')
  var rows = Array.from(tbody.querySelectorAll('tr'))
  rows.sort(function(a, b) {
    var aText = a.cells[col].textContent.trim()
    var bText = b.cells[col].textContent.trim()
    return dir
      ? aText.localeCompare(bText)
      : bText.localeCompare(aText)
  })
  // Clear & re-append sorted
  rows.forEach(function(r) { tbody.appendChild(r) })
  // Update header styles
  var ths = document.querySelectorAll(table + ' th')
  ths.forEach(function(t) { t.classList.remove('sorted') })
  el.classList.add('sorted')
}

    Feature

    Variable-height items arrange themselves automatically. The browser handles all the complex positioning that previously required libraries like Masonry.js or Isotope.

    Note

    Pure CSS. Zero dependencies.

    Layout

    Responsive by nature. Change column-count at breakpoints for different screen sizes. Simple and effective.

    Speed

    No reflow calculations. The browser engine optimizes column layout natively for maximum performance.

    Compat

    Supported in all modern browsers since 2012. A truly battle-tested CSS feature.

    Read More / Truncate zero JS

    __.toggleClass · __.hide · __.show · expand truncated text
    Popstart is an HTML-driven JavaScript library that maps DOM events to function chains via HTML attributes. No build step is required for development. The library was designed with a simple premise: if you can name a function, you can wire it to any DOM event using just HTML attributes. This means designers and developers can collaborate more effectively, prototypes come together faster, and the mental model stays rooted in the document rather than a framework abstraction. Every interaction is declared right where it belongs — on the element itself. The result is code that reads like a blueprint: you see the event, the handler, and the arguments all in one place without hunting through component trees or state management layers.
    HTML
    <div class="readmore-text" id="readmore-text">
  Long content here...
</div>

  ps-click="__.toggleClass, __.hide, __.show"
  toggleClass-selector="#readmore-text" toggleClass-classes="expanded"
  hide-selector="#btn-more" show-selector="#btn-less">Read more</button>

<button class="hidden" id="btn-less"
  ps-click="__.toggleClass, __.hide, __.show"
  toggleClass-selector="#readmore-text" toggleClass-classes="expanded"
  hide-selector="#btn-less" show-selector="#btn-more">Read less</button>

    JavaScript
    function countUp(target, end, duration, prefix) {
  return new Promise(function(resolve) {
    var el = document.querySelector(target)
    var start = 0, startTime = null
    prefix = prefix || ''
    function step(ts) {
      if (!startTime) startTime = ts
      var progress = Math.min((ts - startTime) / duration, 1)
      var ease = 1 - Math.pow(1 - progress, 3)
      var val = Math.floor(ease * end)
      el.textContent = prefix + val.toLocaleString()
      if (progress < 1) requestAnimationFrame(step)
      else resolve()
    }
    requestAnimationFrame(step)
  })
}

    Before / After Slider

    ps-mousedown · drag comparison · clip-path

    <div class="ba-container"
  onmousedown="initCompare(event)"
  ontouchstart="initCompare(event)">
  <div class="ba-layer ba-before">Before</div>

</div>
    JavaScript
    function initCompare(ev) {
  var slider = ev.currentTarget ||
    ev.target.closest('.ba-container')
  var after = slider.querySelector('.ba-after')
  var handle = slider.querySelector('.ba-handle')
  function move(e) {
    var rect = slider.getBoundingClientRect()
    var x = (e.touches ? e.touches[0].clientX : e.clientX)
    var pct = Math.max(0, Math.min(1,
      (x - rect.left) / rect.width)) * 100
    after.style.clipPath =
      'inset(0 0 0 ' + pct + '%)'
    handle.style.left = pct + '%'
  }
  move(ev)
  function up() {
    document.removeEventListener('mousemove', move)
    document.removeEventListener('mouseup', up)
    document.removeEventListener('touchmove', move)
    document.removeEventListener('touchend', up)
  }
  document.addEventListener('mousemove', move)
  document.addEventListener('mouseup', up)
  document.addEventListener('touchmove', move)
  document.addEventListener('touchend', up)
}

    JavaScript
    function tiltMove(e) {
  var el = document.getElementById('tilt-el')
  var r = el.getBoundingClientRect()
  var x = (e.clientX - r.left) / r.width
  var y = (e.clientY - r.top) / r.height
  var rotY = (x - 0.5) * 30
  var rotX = (0.5 - y) * 30
  el.style.transform =
    'rotateX(' + rotX + 'deg) rotateY(' + rotY + 'deg)'
  el.style.setProperty('--tilt-x', (x*100)+'%')
  el.style.setProperty('--tilt-y', (y*100)+'%')
}
function tiltReset() {
  var el = document.getElementById('tilt-el')
  el.style.transform = 'rotateX(0) rotateY(0)'
}

    JavaScript
    function twStart() {
  var text = 'Popstart makes HTML interactive.'
  var el = document.getElementById('tw-output')
  el.textContent = ''
  var i = 0
  return new Promise(function(resolve) {
    var iv = setInterval(function() {
      el.textContent += text[i]
      i++
      if (i >= text.length) { clearInterval(iv); resolve() }
    }, 55)
  })
}

    JavaScript
    var wrWords = ['websites','dashboards','apps','prototypes','UIs']
var wrIdx = 0, wrTimer = null
function wrStart() {
  if (wrTimer) return
  wrTimer = setInterval(function() {
    var el = document.getElementById('wr-word')
    el.classList.add('wr-out')
    el.classList.remove('wr-in')
    setTimeout(function() {
      wrIdx = (wrIdx + 1) % wrWords.length
      el.textContent = wrWords[wrIdx]
      el.classList.remove('wr-out')
      el.classList.add('wr-in')
    }, 300)
  }, 2000)
}
function wrStop() {
  clearInterval(wrTimer); wrTimer = null
}

    function drawSparkline(id, data, color) {
  let w = 120, h = 32, max = Math.max(...data), min = Math.min(...data)
  let pts = data.map((v, i) =>
    [i * (w / (data.length - 1)), h - ((v - min) / (max - min || 1)) * h]
  )
  let d = pts.map((p, i) => (i ? 'L' : 'M') + p[0] + ',' + p[1]).join(' ')
  let el = document.getElementById(id)
  if (el) el.innerHTML = '<svg viewBox="0 0 ' + w + ' ' + h + '">' +
    '<polyline fill="none" stroke="' + color + '" stroke-width="1.5"' +
    ' stroke-linecap="round" points="' +
    pts.map(p => p.join(',')).join(' ') + '"/></svg>'
}

    JavaScript
    var sresActiveCat = 'All', sresViewMode = 'list'
function sresFilter() {
  sresApply(document.getElementById('sres-search')
    .value.toLowerCase())
}
function sresChip(cat) {
  sresActiveCat = cat
  document.querySelectorAll('.sres-chip')
    .forEach(function(c) {
      c.classList.toggle('active',
        c.textContent === cat) })
  sresApply()
}
function sresApplyView(mode) {
  sresViewMode = mode; sresApply()
}
function sresApply(q) {
  q = q || document.getElementById('sres-search')
    .value.toLowerCase()
  // filter both views
  ;['list','grid'].forEach(function(v) {
    var sel = v==='list' ? '.sres-item' : '.sres-gcard'
    var items = document.querySelectorAll(
      '#sres-'+v+'-view ' + sel)
    var count = 0
    items.forEach(function(el) {
      var cat = el.getAttribute('data-scat')
      var txt = el.textContent.toLowerCase()
      var show = (sresActiveCat==='All'
        || cat===sresActiveCat)
        && (!q || txt.indexOf(q) !== -1)
      el.style.display = show ? '' : 'none'
      if (show) count++
    })
  })
}

    JavaScript
    const jvData = {
  name: "Popstart", version: "1.0",
  features: ["events","chaining","DOM watch"],
  config: { debounce: 150, prefix: "ps-" },
  active: true, legacy: null
}
function jvRender(obj, container) {
  container.innerHTML = jvBuild(obj, true)
  container.querySelectorAll('.jv-toggle')
    .forEach(t => t.addEventListener('click',
      () => t.classList.toggle('collapsed')))
}
function jvBuild(val, root) {
  if (val === null) return '<span class="jv-null">null</span>'
  if (typeof val === 'boolean')
    return '<span class="jv-bool">'+val+'</span>'
  if (typeof val === 'number')
    return '<span class="jv-num">'+val+'</span>'
  if (typeof val === 'string')
    return '<span class="jv-str">"'+val+'"</span>'
  // array or object
  let isArr = Array.isArray(val)
  let keys = isArr ? val : Object.keys(val)
  let open = isArr ? '[' : '{'
  let close = isArr ? ']' : '}'
  let n = isArr ? val.length : keys.length
  let html = '<span class="jv-toggle">'
    + '<span class="jv-brace">'+open+'</span>'
    + ' <span class="jv-count">'+n+' items</span>'
    + '</span><div class="jv-node">'
  let entries = isArr ? val : keys
  entries.forEach((k,i) => {
    let v = isArr ? k : val[k]
    let comma = i < entries.length-1 ? ',' : ''
    if (!isArr) html += '<span class="jv-key">"'+k+'"</span>: '
    html += jvBuild(v)
      + '<span class="jv-comma">'+comma+'</span><br>'
  })
  html += '</div><span class="jv-brace">'+close+'</span>'
  return html
}
jvRender(jvData, document.getElementById('jv-tree'))

    CSS
    @keyframes ds-fadeSlideUp {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(18px) }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0) }
}
.ds-card { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(18px) }
.ds-row.ds-animated .ds-card {
  animation: ds-fadeSlideUp 0.6s ease forwards;
}
/* staggered delay per card */
.ds-row.ds-animated .ds-card:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 0.1s }
.ds-row.ds-animated .ds-card:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 0.2s }
.ds-row.ds-animated .ds-card:nth-child(4) { animation-delay: 0.3s }
/* sparkline bars grow from bottom */
.ds-spark span {
  transform-origin: bottom;
  transform: scaleY(0);
  transition: transform 0.8s ease;
}
.ds-row.ds-animated .ds-spark span {
  transform: scaleY(1);
}
    JavaScript
    // Count-up animation triggered by IntersectionObserver
function animateDashStats(row) {
  row.classList.add('ds-animated')  // triggers CSS fade-in
  row.querySelectorAll('.ds-value').forEach(function(el) {
    var match = el.textContent.match(/^([^0-9]*?)([\d,.]+)(.*)$/)
    var num = parseFloat(match[2].replace(/,/g, ''))
    var start = performance.now()
    requestAnimationFrame(function tick(now) {
      var t = Math.min((now - start) / 1500, 1)
      var ease = 1 - Math.pow(1 - t, 3)  // easeOutCubic
      el.textContent = match[1]
        + Math.round(ease * num).toLocaleString()
        + match[3]
      if (t < 1) requestAnimationFrame(tick)
    })
  })
}
// observe, animate once visible
new IntersectionObserver(function(entries, obs) {
  entries.forEach(function(e) {
    if (e.isIntersecting) {
      animateDashStats(e.target)
      obs.unobserve(e.target)
    }
  })
}, {threshold: 0.2}).observe(dsRow)

    JavaScript
    function gaugeSet(value) {
  var v = parseInt(value), pct = v / 100
  var arc = 283, offset = arc - (pct * arc)
  var fill = document.getElementById('gauge-fill')
  fill.style.strokeDashoffset = offset
  // Color: green(good) → orange(mid) → red(low)
  var hue = pct * 120  // 0=red 60=yellow 120=green
  fill.style.stroke = 'hsl('+hue+',70%,50%)'
  // Needle: -90deg(0%) to +90deg(100%)
  var angle = -90 + (pct * 180)
  var needle = document.getElementById('gauge-needle')
  needle.setAttribute('transform',
    'rotate('+angle+',110,110)')
  document.getElementById('gauge-val').textContent = v
}

    JavaScript
    let cdSec = 300, cdTimer = null
function fmtTime(s) {
  return String(Math.floor(s/60)).padStart(2,'0')
    + ':' + String(s%60).padStart(2,'0')
}
function startCountdown() {
  if (cdTimer) return
  cdTimer = setInterval(() => {
    cdSec--
    __.text('#countdown', fmtTime(cdSec))
    if (cdSec <= 0) { clearInterval(cdTimer); cdTimer = null }
  }, 1000)
}
function resetCountdown() {
  clearInterval(cdTimer); cdTimer = null
  cdSec = 300; __.text('#countdown', fmtTime(cdSec))
}

    JavaScript
    let tagId = 2
function addTag(ev) {
  if (ev.key !== 'Enter' && ev.key !== ',') return
  let val = ev.target.value.replace(/,/g,'').trim()
  if (!val) { ev.target.value = ''; return }
  let id = 'tag-' + (++tagId)
  __.before(ev.target,
    '<span class="tag" id="' + id + '">'
    + __.safify(val)
    + ' <span class="tag-x" ps-click="__.del"'
    + ' del-selector="#' + id + '">×</span>'
    + '</span>')
  ev.target.value = ''
  __.Popstart()
}

    Toast Stack

    __.append · __.del · auto-dismiss stacking toasts

    Toasts appear at bottom-right and auto-dismiss after 3 seconds.

    CSS
    /* Fixed container in the bottom-right corner */
.toast-zone {
  position: fixed;
  bottom: 1.5rem;
  right: 1.5rem;
  z-index: 300;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 0.5rem;
  pointer-events: none;
}

/* Individual toast */
.toast {
  padding: 0.65rem 1.1rem;
  background: var(--card, #1c2028);
  border: 1px solid var(--card-border, rgba(255,255,255,0.08));
  border-radius: 8px;
  box-shadow: 0 4px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3);
  font-size: 13px;
  color: var(--fg, #e8e4df);
  pointer-events: auto;
  animation: toastIn .3s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
  max-width: 320px;
  transition: opacity .4s, transform .4s;
}

/* Status variants -- colored border + text */
.toast.success { border-color: var(--success, #3cb88a); color: var(--success, #3cb88a); }
.toast.error   { border-color: var(--error, #e8465a);   color: var(--error, #e8465a); }
.toast.info    { border-color: var(--info, #5aaddd);    color: var(--info, #5aaddd); }

/* Fade-out class added before removal */
.toast.fade-out { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(40px); }

@keyframes toastIn {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(40px); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
}

    JavaScript
    // Toast counter for unique IDs
let toastId = 0

function showToast(msg, type) {
  let id = 'toast-' + (++toastId)

  // __.append injects HTML into #toast-zone
  // __.safify escapes the message to prevent XSS
  __.append('#toast-zone',
    '<div class="toast ' + (type || '') + '" id="' + id + '">'
    + __.safify(msg) + '</div>')

  // Auto-dismiss: fade out, then remove from DOM
  setTimeout(function() {
    var t = document.getElementById(id)
    if (t) {
      t.classList.add('fade-out')
      setTimeout(function() { t.remove() }, 400)
    }
  }, 3000)
}

    JavaScript
    function spStepTo(step) {
  step = parseInt(step)
  for (let i = 1; i <= 4; i++) {
    let node = document.getElementById('sn-' + i)
    let line = document.getElementById('sl-' + i)
    node.className = 'step-node'
    if (i < step) {
      node.classList.add('step-complete')
      node.querySelector('.step-circle').innerHTML = '&#10003;'
    } else if (i === step) {
      node.classList.add('step-active')
      node.querySelector('.step-circle').textContent = i
    } else {
      node.querySelector('.step-circle').textContent = i
    }
    if (line) line.className = 'step-line' + (i < step ? ' step-done' : '')
  }
}

    JavaScript
    function fireConfetti() {
  let zone = document.getElementById('confetti-zone')
  let colors = ['var(--accent)','var(--success)',
    'var(--error)','var(--warning)','var(--info)']
  for (let i=0; i<30; i++) {
    let p = document.createElement('div')
    p.className = 'confetti-piece'
    p.style.left = Math.random()*90+5 + '%'
    p.style.background = colors[i%colors.length]
    p.style.animationDelay = Math.random()*0.4+'s'
    p.style.animationDuration = 0.8+Math.random()*0.8+'s'
    zone.appendChild(p)
    setTimeout(() => p.remove(), 2000)
  }
}

    Scroll Progress

    onscroll · reading progress bar

    Chapter 1: The Beginning

    In the world of web development, interactivity has always been the bridge between static content and dynamic experiences. For decades, developers have relied on complex frameworks to make their pages come alive.

    Chapter 2: A New Approach

    But what if the HTML itself could declare its behavior? What if every click, every input, every change could be mapped directly in the markup? This is the philosophy behind attribute-driven development.

    Chapter 3: The Power of Simplicity

    When you remove the layers of abstraction, something remarkable happens. The code becomes readable, maintainable, and accessible to developers of all skill levels. No build steps, no dependency trees, no configuration files.

    Chapter 4: Looking Forward

    The future belongs to tools that respect the platform. HTML was designed to be declarative. CSS was designed to be declarative. Perhaps it is time for our interactivity layer to follow suit.

    Epilogue

    And so we return to the fundamentals. One script tag. A few attributes. And the entire power of JavaScript at your fingertips, mapped cleanly to the elements that need it.

    function spUpdate(el) {
  var pct = el.scrollTop /
    (el.scrollHeight - el.clientHeight) * 100
  el.closest('.sp-wrapper')
    .querySelector('.sp-fill')
    .style.width = pct + '%'
}

    JavaScript
    let upTimers = {}
function simulateUpload(barId, pctId, speed) {
  let pct = 0
  upTimers[barId] = setInterval(() => {
    pct += Math.random() * (speed || 3) + 1
    if (pct >= 100) {
      pct = 100; clearInterval(upTimers[barId])
      let bar = document.getElementById(barId)
      if (bar) { bar.classList.remove('uploading'); bar.classList.add('done') }
    }
    let bar = document.getElementById(barId)
    let label = document.getElementById(pctId)
    if (bar) bar.style.width = pct + '%'
    if (label) label.textContent = Math.round(pct) + '%'
  }, 120)
}
function startUploads() {
  resetUploads()
  simulateUpload('up-bar-1','up-pct-1', 2)
  simulateUpload('up-bar-2','up-pct-2', 5)
  simulateUpload('up-bar-3','up-pct-3', 15)
}
function cancelUpload(fid) {
  let idx = fid.replace('up-file-','')
  clearInterval(upTimers['up-bar-'+idx])
  let bar = document.getElementById('up-bar-'+idx)
  if (bar) { bar.classList.remove('uploading'); bar.classList.add('error') }
  __.text('#up-pct-'+idx, 'cancelled')
}
function resetUploads() {
  Object.values(upTimers).forEach(t => clearInterval(t))
  upTimers = {};
  [1,2,3].forEach(i => {
    let bar = document.getElementById('up-bar-'+i)
    if (bar) { bar.style.width='0%'; bar.className='up-fill uploading' }
    __.text('#up-pct-'+i, '0%')
  })
}

    <div class="mp-progress" ps-click="mpSeek">
  <div class="mp-progress-fill" id="mp-fill"></div>
</div>
<button ps-click="mpToggle">▶</button>
<button ps-click="mpPrev">⏮</button>

    JavaScript
    var mpTracks = [
  {title:'Midnight Drive', dur:204},
  {title:'Neon City', dur:186},
  {title:'Retro Sunset', dur:237}
]
var mpIdx=0, mpPos=0, mpTimer=null, mpPlaying=false
function mpFmt(s) {
  return Math.floor(s/60)+':'
    +String(Math.floor(s)%60).padStart(2,'0')
}
function mpUpdate() {
  var t=mpTracks[mpIdx], pct=(mpPos/t.dur)*100
  __.css('#mp-fill','width:'+pct+'%')
  __.text('#mp-current', mpFmt(mpPos))
}
function mpToggle() {
  mpPlaying = !mpPlaying
  __.text('#mp-play-btn', mpPlaying?'❚❚':'▶')
  if (mpPlaying) mpTimer = setInterval(function(){
    mpPos += 0.25; if (mpPos >= mpTracks[mpIdx].dur) mpNext()
    mpUpdate()
  }, 250)
  else clearInterval(mpTimer)
}
function mpNext() {
  clearInterval(mpTimer); mpPlaying=false; mpPos=0
  mpIdx = (mpIdx+1) % mpTracks.length; mpLoad()
}
function mpPrev() {
  clearInterval(mpTimer); mpPlaying=false; mpPos=0
  mpIdx = (mpIdx-1+mpTracks.length) % mpTracks.length; mpLoad()
}
function mpLoad() {
  var t=mpTracks[mpIdx]
  __.text('#mp-track-title', t.title)
  __.text('#mp-total', mpFmt(t.dur))
  __.text('#mp-play-btn', '▶'); mpUpdate()
}
function mpSeek(ev) {
  var bar = document.getElementById('mp-progress-bar')
  var rect = bar.getBoundingClientRect()
  var pct = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width
  mpPos = pct * mpTracks[mpIdx].dur; mpUpdate()
}

    Text & Visual

    Text Truncation zero JS

    __.toggleClass · expand/collapse long text
    Popstart is an HTML-driven JavaScript library that maps DOM events to function chains via HTML attributes. No build step is required for development. Simply include the script tag and start wiring up your interactive components using declarative attributes. The library uses a promise-based execution chain, so each function in the chain runs sequentially, and if any function rejects, the chain stops and the error handler runs. This makes it incredibly easy to compose complex interactive behaviors from simple, reusable functions without writing any custom JavaScript glue code. The entire paradigm shifts from imperative event handling to declarative HTML attributes.

  Long paragraph text here...

  toggleClass-selector="#trunc-text-1"
  toggleClass-classes="trunc-expanded">Show More / Less</button>
    CSS
    .trunc-text {
  -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  display: -webkit-box;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.trunc-text.trunc-expanded {
  -webkit-line-clamp: unset;
  display: block;

    Popstart Documentation

    Popstart is an HTML-driven JavaScript library that maps DOM events to function chains via HTML attributes. No build step, no virtual DOM, no framework lock-in — just attributes.

    Installation

    Include the scripts in your HTML. Core is required; extras and plugins are optional.

    <!-- Core: event binding, function chaining, DOM utilities -->
<script src="popstart-core.js"></script>

<!-- Extras: HTTP, forms, alerts, cookies, storage, streaming -->
<script src="popstart-extras.js"></script>

<!-- Plugins: router, drag & drop (lazy-loaded) -->
<script src="popstart-plugins.js"></script>

    Your First Interactive Element

    Add a ps-click attribute to any element. The value is the function to call when clicked.

    <button ps-click="sayHello">Click Me</button>

<script>
function sayHello(el) {
  el.textContent = 'Hello, Popstart!'
}
</script>

    That's it. No initialization code, no event listeners to wire up, no framework to configure. Popstart finds the attribute on DOMContentLoaded and binds the click event automatically.

    How It Works (30-Second Version)

    1. Popstart scans the DOM for elements with event attributes like ps-click, ps-submit, ps-change
    2. When the event fires, Popstart finds the named function, reads arguments from attributes, and calls it
    3. Multiple functions are chained as a sequential promise chain: ps-click="fn1, fn2, fn3"
    4. Built-in functions on the __ object handle common tasks: show/hide, AJAX, forms, alerts
    Tip: You can use four attribute prefixes interchangeably: ps-click (recommended), click, data-click, or x-click. Popstart checks them in that order and uses the first match.

    A More Complete Example

    Here is a complete form that validates, scrapes form data, posts to an API, and shows a success message — with zero custom JavaScript:

    <script src="popstart-core.js"></script>
<script src="popstart-extras.js"></script>

<form ps-submit="__.validate, __.scrape, __.post, __.alertSuccess"
  post-url="/api/contact"
  alertSuccess-msg="Message sent!"
  post-error="__.alertError">

  <input name="email" type="email" required placeholder="Your email">
  <textarea name="message" required placeholder="Your message"></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>

    The chain __.validate → __.scrape → __.post → __.alertSuccess runs sequentially. If validation fails, the chain stops. If the POST fails, __.alertError handles it.

    Core Concepts

    The mental model: HTML attributes declare behavior. Functions execute. Promises chain.

    Event Attributes

    The attribute name is ps- plus the DOM event name. The value is one or more function names to call.

    AttributeFires When
    ps-clickElement is clicked
    ps-submitForm is submitted
    ps-changeInput value changes (and loses focus, or for checkboxes/selects)
    ps-keyupKey is released in input
    ps-inputInput value changes (real-time, every keystroke)
    ps-mouseupMouse button is released
    ps-startup / startupPage loads (DOMContentLoaded)
    <button ps-click="save">Save</button>
<input ps-change="validate">
<form ps-submit="handleSubmit">
<div startup="loadConfig">
    Default events: click, mouseup, change, input, keyup, submit. You can add more via __.config.BoundEventNames.push('mouseover').

    Function Chaining

    Comma-separated function names execute as a sequential promise chain. Each function must resolve before the next one starts. If any function rejects, the chain stops and the error handler runs.

    <button ps-click="validate, save, __.alertSuccess"
  alertSuccess-msg="Done!">Submit</button>

    The chain above runs: validate() → then save() → then __.alertSuccess("Done!"). Both synchronous functions and functions that return Promises work in chains.

    Argument Mapping

    Popstart reads your function's parameter names and looks for matching attributes on the element. The pattern is {functionName}-{paramName}="value".

    <button ps-click="fetchData"
  fetchData-url="/api/users"
  fetchData-method="GET">Fetch</button>

<script>
function fetchData(url, method) {
  // url = "/api/users", method = "GET"
  return fetch(url, { method })
}
</script>

    Special Parameter Names

    These parameter names are auto-injected without needing attributes:

    Parameter NameReceives
    el, ele, elementThe DOM element that triggered the event
    ev, evt, eventThe DOM Event object
    <div ps-click="highlight">Click me</div>

<script>
function highlight(el) {
  el.style.background = 'yellow'  // el = the clicked div
}
</script>
    Note: All argument values from attributes are strings. Your function receives string values; parse them as needed (e.g., parseInt(count)).

    The __ Object

    The double-underscore object (__) is Popstart's global namespace. It contains:

    • __.data — shared data store between function calls
    • __.state — runtime state (last result, last event, last element)
    • __.config — configuration options
    • All built-in functions: __.show(), __.get(), __.scrape(), etc.

    To call a built-in function from an attribute, use the __. prefix:

    <button ps-click="__.show"
  show-selector="#panel">Show Panel</button>

    Suffix Pattern

    To call the same function multiple times in one chain, append -N (dash + number) as a suffix. Arguments use the same suffix:

    <button ps-click="__.get-1, __.get-2"
  get-url-1="/api/users"
  get-writedatapath-1="users"
  get-url-2="/api/roles"
  get-writedatapath-2="roles">Load Both</button>

    Function names that naturally end in digits (like handler2) are not treated as suffixed.

    Error Handling

    Set a per-function error handler with {functionName}-error="handlerName". When a function rejects, the chain stops and the error handler runs.

    <button ps-click="__.post, __.alertSuccess"
  post-url="/api/save"
  post-error="__.alertError"
  alertSuccess-msg="Saved!">Save</button>

    The fallback chain is: per-function fn-error → element-level error attribute → __.error() (default handler).

    Error handlers are exit ramps, not recovery. After the error handler runs, the chain is done. If you need to branch to a different flow, use __.trigger() from inside your error handler to fire a new chain on another element.

    Event Control

    By default, click, submit, change, and mouseup events get preventDefault() and stopPropagation() called automatically. Override per-element:

    <!-- Let the default link behavior happen -->
<a ps-click="trackClick"
   ps-click-prevent-default="false"
   href="/about">About</a>

    Startup Events

    The startup, startup1, and startup2 attributes run their function chains on DOMContentLoaded:

    <div startup="loadConfig"
  loadConfig-url="/api/config"></div>

    Startup functions receive a synthetic event {type:"startup"}, not a real DOM Event.

    Function Lookup

    Popstart checks the __ namespace first, then window. Dot notation works for nested objects:

    <!-- Finds window.app.save -->
<button ps-click="app.save">Save</button>

<!-- Finds __.redirect -->
<button ps-click="__.redirect"
  redirect-url="/home">Go Home</button>

    Data Persistence

    Return values from functions are stored in __.data["functionPath"]. Use the writedatapath attribute for a custom key:

    <div startup="loadUser"
  loadUser-url="/api/me"
  loadUser-writedatapath="currentUser"></div>

<script>
function loadUser(url) {
  return fetch(url).then(r => r.json())
  // Result stored in __.data.currentUser
}
</script>

    Read stored data with readdatapath in functions like __.post, __.populate, etc. undefined return values are not stored; 0, false, null, "" are stored.

    Debounce

    Events are debounced by default to prevent double-fires. Override per-element:

    EventDefault Debounce
    click, mouseup50ms
    input, change, keyup300ms
    <!-- Custom debounce -->
<input ps-keyup="search" debounce="500">

<!-- Disable debounce -->
<button ps-click="fire" debounce="0">Instant</button>

    DOM Manipulation

    Built-in functions for showing, hiding, styling, and modifying DOM elements. All are on the __ object (core).

    Core

    Visibility

    __.show(selector)
    Shows element(s) by removing the .hidden class and clearing display:none. When called without a selector from a chain, operates on the triggering element.
    <button ps-click="__.show" show-selector="#panel">Show</button>
<div class="hidden" id="panel">Now visible</div>
    __.hide(selector)
    Hides element(s) by adding .hidden class and setting display:none.
    <button ps-click="__.hide" hide-selector="#panel">Hide</button>
    __.toggle(selector)
    Toggles visibility. If hidden, shows it; if visible, hides it.
    <button ps-click="__.toggle" toggle-selector="#menu">Menu</button>

    Class Manipulation

    __.addClass(selector, classes)
    Adds one or more CSS classes (space or comma separated). Accepts classes with or without leading dots.
    <button ps-click="__.addClass"
  addClass-selector="#box" addClass-classes="highlight active">Activate</button>
    __.removeClass(selector, classes)
    Removes one or more CSS classes.
    __.toggleClass(selector, classes)
    Toggles one or more CSS classes on/off.
    <div ps-click="__.toggleClass" toggleClass-classes="on">Toggle me</div>
    __.hasClass(selector, cls) → boolean
    Returns true if any matched element has the class.

    Content

    __.text(selector, content)
    Gets or sets textContent. Omit content to get. Safe from XSS since it sets text, not HTML.
    <button ps-click="__.text"
  text-selector="#output" text-content="Updated!">Set Text</button>
    __.html(selector, content)
    Gets or sets innerHTML. Does not auto-sanitize — use __.safify() on user data.
    __.val(selector, value)
    Gets or sets an input's value.

    Attributes & Styles

    __.attr(selector, name, value)
    Gets or sets an HTML attribute. Also handles style as a special case (gets/sets cssText).
    __.css(selector, prop, value)
    Gets or sets CSS. __.css(sel, 'color') reads. __.css(sel, 'color', 'red') writes. __.css(sel, {color:'red', fontSize:'16px'}) writes multiple.
    __.prop(selector, name, value)
    Gets or sets a DOM property (e.g., disabled, checked).

    DOM Insertion

    __.append(selector, html)
    Inserts HTML at the end of element(s) (inside, after existing content).
    __.prepend(selector, html)
    Inserts HTML at the beginning of element(s).
    __.before(selector, html)
    Inserts HTML before the element (as a sibling).
    __.after(selector, html)
    Inserts HTML after the element (as a sibling).
    __.replace(selector, html)
    Replaces the element with new HTML content.

    DOM Removal & Cloning

    __.empty(selector)
    Clears all inner content of element(s).
    __.del(selector)
    Removes element(s) from the DOM entirely.
    <span>Tag <span ps-click="__.del">&times;</span></span>
    __.clone(selector, deep) → Node
    Clones the first matched element. deep defaults to true.
    __.create(tag, attrs, content) → Element
    Creates a new element. attrs is an object of attribute name/value pairs.
    let btn = __.create('button', {class: 'btn'}, 'Click me')

    DOM Traversal

    __.el(selector, container) → Element[]
    Query selector shorthand. Always returns an array. Accepts selectors, Elements, or arrays. Optional container limits scope.
    __.closest(selector, match) → Element|null
    Finds the closest ancestor matching match.
    __.parent(selector) → Element|null
    Returns the parent element.
    __.children(selector, filter) → Element[]
    Returns child elements. Optional filter selector narrows results.
    __.siblings(selector) → Element[]
    Returns sibling elements (excluding the element itself).
    __.next(selector) → Element|null
    Returns the next sibling element.
    __.prev(selector) → Element|null
    Returns the previous sibling element.

    Security

    __.safify(str) → string
    HTML-escapes a string to prevent XSS. Upgrades to DOMPurify if loaded. Always call this when interpolating user data into HTML:
    __.append('#list', '<li>' + __.safify(userData.name) + '</li>')

    Navigation & Switching

    One-line helpers for tabs, accordions, navigation patterns, and page transitions.

    switchTo

    __.switchTo(show, hide, siblings, cls)
    The workhorse for tabs, radio selection, and nav patterns. Hides hide elements, shows show element, removes cls (default "active") from siblings, adds cls to the clicked element.
    <!-- Tab bar -->
<div class="tab-bar">
  <button ps-click="__.switchTo" class="btn active"
    switchTo-show="#tab-1" switchTo-hide=".tab-panel"
    switchTo-siblings=".tab-bar .btn" debounce="0">Tab 1</button>
  <button ps-click="__.switchTo" class="btn"
    switchTo-show="#tab-2" switchTo-hide=".tab-panel"
    switchTo-siblings=".tab-bar .btn" debounce="0">Tab 2</button>
</div>
<div id="tab-1" class="tab-panel">Content 1</div>
<div id="tab-2" class="tab-panel hidden">Content 2</div>
    Tip: __.switchTo adds the class to this (the clicked element). This makes it perfect for highlighting the active tab/button without any JavaScript.
    Extras

    togglePanel

    __.togglePanel(selector, cls)
    Accordion and tree view toggle. Toggles visibility of selector and toggles cls (default "open") on the clicked element. The open class lets you style the trigger (e.g., rotate a chevron).
    <button ps-click="__.togglePanel"
  togglePanel-selector="#faq-1">Is it hard? ▼</button>
<div class="hidden" id="faq-1">No — just one attribute.</div>

    Scroll & Redirect

    __.scrollTo(selector)
    Smooth-scrolls to the first matched element using scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'}).
    <a ps-click="__.scrollTo"
  scrollTo-selector="#contact">Jump to Contact</a>
    __.redirect(url)
    Navigates the browser to a new URL by setting document.location.
    <button ps-click="save, __.redirect"
  redirect-url="/dashboard">Save & Go</button>
    Extras
    __.historyPush(url)
    Pushes a URL to the browser history without navigating (SPA-style).
    __.historyReplace(url)
    Replaces the current history entry without navigating.
    __.back()
    Goes back one step in browser history.

    Conditional Visibility

    __.showIf(selector, readdatapath, value)
    Shows selector if __.data[readdatapath] matches value (or is truthy when value is omitted). Hides otherwise. Never breaks the chain.
    __.hideIf(selector, readdatapath, value)
    Hides selector if the data matches. Shows otherwise.
    __.toggleIf(selector, readdatapath, value)
    Shows if match, hides if not. Same as __.showIf.

    Feedback & Alerts

    Visual feedback functions for success/error messages, loading states, and temporary effects.

    Extras

    Alert Banners

    Top-of-page banners that auto-dismiss. They stack and can be closed manually.

    __.alertSuccess(msg, timeout)
    Green success banner. Default timeout: 15 seconds.
    <button ps-click="save, __.alertSuccess"
  alertSuccess-msg="Changes saved!">Save</button>
    __.alertError(msg, timeout)
    Red error banner. Great as an error handler in chains.
    <button ps-click="__.post"
  post-url="/api/save" post-error="__.alertError">Save</button>
    __.alertWarning(msg, timeout)
    Amber warning banner.
    __.alertInfo(msg, timeout)
    Blue informational banner.
    __.alert(msg, classes, timeout)
    Base alert function. classes customizes appearance (e.g., "success", "error").
    __.alertClose()
    Immediately dismisses any visible alert.

    Loading States

    __.loading(selector, loadingtext)
    Adds .loading class, disables the element, and optionally swaps text. Saves original state for __.done().
    <button ps-click="__.loading, __.post, __.done"
  loading-selector="#save-btn" loading-loadingtext="Saving..."
  post-url="/api/save"
  done-selector="#save-btn" id="save-btn">Save</button>
    __.done(selector, donetext)
    Reverses __.loading() — removes .loading class, re-enables, restores original text (or sets donetext).

    Temporary Effects

    __.timedclass(selector, removeclassname, addclassname, time)
    Temporarily swaps classes: removes removeclassname, adds addclassname, then reverses after time ms (default 2000). Forces CSS reflow so animations always restart. Useful for shake, flash, or pulse effects.
    <button ps-click="__.timedclass"
  timedclass-selector="#box"
  timedclass-addclassname="flash"
  timedclass-time="1000">Flash It</button>

    Error Display

    __.error(msg)
    Default error handler. Looks for a .error-msg element first, then falls back to an alert banner. This is the fallback when no fn-error attribute is set.
    __.displayError(msg, selector)
    Shows error text in a .error-msg element (or custom selector), auto-hides after 10 seconds.
    __.clearError(selector)
    Hides the error message element.

    Utility Functions

    General-purpose helpers for event control, timing, clipboard, and more.

    Core
    __.noop()
    Does nothing. Useful for stopping event propagation on nested elements (e.g., a modal box inside a backdrop). When Popstart calls a function on an element, the event is stopped — __.noop exploits this.
    <!-- Backdrop click closes modal, inner noop prevents close -->
<div class="modal-bg" ps-click="closeModal">
  <div class="modal-box" ps-click="__.noop" debounce="0">
    Modal content...
  </div>
</div>
    __.delay(time) → Promise
    Pauses the chain for time ms (default 1000). Returns a promise that resolves after the delay.
    <button ps-click="__.alertInfo, __.delay, __.alertClose"
  alertInfo-msg="Wait for it..." delay-time="2000">Demo</button>
    __.trigger(selector, event)
    Programmatically fires a Popstart event on element(s). This calls __.PopEvent directly, so it triggers the full chain machinery.
    <button ps-click="__.trigger"
  trigger-selector="#hidden-form" trigger-event="submit">Submit Form</button>
    Extras
    __.copy(text) → Promise
    Copies text to the clipboard. Uses navigator.clipboard with fallback to execCommand.
    <button ps-click="__.copy, __.alertSuccess"
  copy-text="Copied text!" alertSuccess-msg="Copied!">Copy</button>
    __.enable(selector)
    Enables element(s): sets disabled = false and removes the .disabled class.
    __.disable(selector)
    Disables element(s): sets disabled = true and adds the .disabled class.
    __.focus(selector)
    Sets keyboard focus to the first matched element.
    __.uuid() → string
    Generates a UUID v4 string. Uses crypto.randomUUID() with fallback.
    __.template(str, data) → string
    Simple mustache-style template: replaces {key} placeholders in str with values from data (defaults to __.data).

    Conditional Gates

    These resolve or reject based on __.data values, allowing conditional chain execution.

    __.succeedIf(readdatapath, value) → Promise
    Resolves if __.data[readdatapath] matches value (or is truthy). Rejects otherwise — stopping the chain.
    <button ps-click="__.succeedIf, deleteItem"
  succeedIf-readdatapath="user.isAdmin"
  succeedIf-value="true">Delete (admin only)</button>
    __.failIf(readdatapath, value) → Promise
    Rejects if __.data[readdatapath] matches value. Resolves otherwise.
    __.succeedIfCookie(name, value) → Promise
    Resolves if the named cookie equals value. Rejects otherwise.
    __.failIfCookie(name, value) → Promise
    Rejects if the named cookie equals value. Resolves otherwise.

    Data & State

    Storage functions for sharing data between functions, persisting to localStorage/sessionStorage, and managing the data store.

    The Data Store

    __.data is a plain JavaScript object that acts as Popstart's shared data store. Function return values are automatically stored here, and data-aware functions read from it.

    // Automatic storage after function execution:
// If fetchUsers() returns [{name:"Alice"}, ...],
// __.data["fetchUsers"] holds the result.

// Custom key with writedatapath:
// get-writedatapath="users" stores in __.data.users

// Read with readdatapath:
// populate-readdatapath="users" reads from __.data.users
    Extras

    localStorage

    __.store(key, value)
    Versatile localStorage wrapper with auto-JSON:
    • __.store("user") — get (auto-parses JSON)
    • __.store("user", {name:"Alice"}) — set (auto-stringifies)
    • __.store("user", null) — remove
    <button ps-click="__.store"
  store-key="theme" store-value="dark">Save Theme</button>

    sessionStorage

    __.session(key, value)
    Same API as __.store() but uses sessionStorage (cleared when the browser tab closes).

    URL Arguments

    __.argsParse(writedatapath)
    Parses URL query parameters into __.data.args (or a custom path). For example, ?id=42&name=foo becomes __.data.args = {id: "42", name: "foo"}.
    <div startup="__.argsParse"></div>
<!-- Now __.data.args has all query params -->
    __.requireArg(name, writedatapath) → Promise
    Requires a URL query parameter. Resolves with the value if present; rejects with an error message if missing. Stores the value in __.data.arg[name].

    Runtime State

    Popstart tracks runtime state in __.state:

    PathContains
    __.state.lastOp.lastReturn value of the last function executed
    __.state.lastOp.evThe last event object
    __.state.lastOp.thisThe last element that triggered an event

    Forms

    Validate, extract, populate, and reset form data — all wirable from HTML attributes.

    Extras
    __.validate(selector) → Promise
    HTML5 constraint validation. Resolves if the form is valid; rejects if invalid (stopping the chain). Calls reportValidity() to show browser validation messages.
    <form ps-submit="__.validate, __.scrape, __.post"
  post-url="/api/submit">
  <input name="email" type="email" required>
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
    __.scrape(selector, writeDataPath) → object
    Extracts all input values from a form (or container) as a flat object. Stores the result in __.data.form (or custom writeDataPath). Handles checkboxes (boolean), radios, multi-selects, text inputs, and textareas.
    <!-- Scrape and display form data -->
<form ps-submit="__.scrape" id="my-form">
  <input name="firstName" value="Jane">
  <input name="lastName" value="Doe">
</form>
<!-- __.data.form = { firstName: "Jane", lastName: "Doe" } -->
    __.populate(selector, readdatapath)
    Fills form inputs from __.data. Matches input name attributes to data keys. Handles checkboxes, radios, multi-selects. Also fills [populate="key"] elements with text content and processes [populate-html] templates. Fires a populated event on the container.
    <form startup="loadUser, __.populate"
  loadUser-writedatapath="user"
  populate-readdatapath="user">
  <input name="email">
  <input name="name">
  <span populate="role"></span>
</form>
    __.resetForm(selector)
    Resets form inputs to their default values. Calls form.reset() or finds a <form> within the container.
    The classic chain: ps-submit="__.validate, __.scrape, __.post, __.alertSuccess" — validates the form, scrapes all inputs into __.data.form, POSTs it to the server, then shows a success message. If any step fails, the chain stops.

    HTTP

    Fetch wrappers with automatic JSON handling, error throwing, and integration with the data store.

    Extras

    Request Methods

    __.get(url, data, readdatapath, headers) → Promise
    GET request. data is appended as query parameters. If no data attribute is set, reads from __.data.form (so __.scrape, __.get just works). Auto-parses JSON responses.
    <div startup="__.get"
  get-url="/api/users"
  get-writedatapath="users"></div>
    __.post(url, data, readdatapath, headers) → Promise
    POST request with JSON body. If no data attribute, reads from __.data.form. Sets Content-Type: application/json automatically.
    <form ps-submit="__.scrape, __.post, __.alertSuccess"
  post-url="/api/items"
  alertSuccess-msg="Created!"
  post-error="__.alertError">
  <input name="title" required>
  <button type="submit">Create</button>
</form>
    __.put(url, data, readdatapath, headers) → Promise
    PUT request. Same conventions as __.post.
    __.patch(url, data, readdatapath, headers) → Promise
    PATCH request. Same conventions as __.post.
    __.delete(url, headers) → Promise
    DELETE request. No body. Returns parsed response.
    __.head(url, headers) → Promise
    HEAD request.
    __.options(url, headers) → Promise
    OPTIONS request (CORS preflight check).
    __.http(url, method, data, readdatapath, headers) → Promise
    Low-level HTTP function. All other methods delegate to this. Set method to any HTTP verb.

    HTML Fetching

    __.getHTML(url, selector)
    Fetches HTML from a URL and injects it into the target element. HTMX-style server-rendered partial loading.
    <div startup="__.getHTML"
  getHTML-url="/partials/sidebar.html"
  getHTML-selector="#sidebar"></div>

    File Upload

    __.upload(url, selector, name) → Promise
    POSTs file(s) via FormData. Auto-finds input[type=file] within the selector. name defaults to the input's name attribute or "file".
    <input type="file" name="avatar">
<button ps-click="__.upload"
  upload-url="/api/upload">Upload</button>

    Default Headers

    Set __.config.httpHeaders to include headers with every request (e.g., auth tokens):

    __.config.httpHeaders = {
  'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + token,
  'X-Custom-Header': 'value'
}

    Data Rendering

    Render arrays and objects into DOM elements using templates.

    Extras

    populateEach

    __.populateEach(selector, readdatapath, valuefield, labelfield, append)
    Renders an array from __.data as repeated HTML. Uses a <template> inside the target with {key} placeholders. For <select> elements, auto-builds <option> tags. Fires a populated event when done. Data values are auto-sanitized when __.config.sanitize is true.

    List/Card Rendering

    Place a <template> inside the target element. {key} placeholders are replaced with values from each array item:

    <ul id="users">
  <template><li>{name} &mdash; {email}</li></template>
</ul>

<div startup="__.get, __.populateEach"
  get-url="/api/users"
  get-writedatapath="users"
  populateEach-selector="#users"
  populateEach-readdatapath="users"></div>

    Select Dropdown

    For <select> elements, populateEach builds <option> tags automatically. Use valuefield and labelfield for object arrays:

    <select id="roles"><option value="">Pick a role...</option></select>

<div startup="__.get, __.populateEach"
  get-url="/api/roles" get-writedatapath="roles"
  populateEach-selector="#roles"
  populateEach-readdatapath="roles"
  populateEach-valuefield="id"
  populateEach-labelfield="name"></div>
    Tip: The first <option> with no value is preserved as a placeholder. Set append="true" to add to existing content instead of replacing.

    populate

    __.populate(selector, readdatapath)
    Fills individual inputs and display elements from a data object. Three modes:
    • Form inputs: matches name attribute to data keys
    • Display elements: [populate="key"] sets innerHTML to the value
    • Templates: [populate-html] replaces {key} placeholders in the element's HTML

    template

    __.template(str, data) → string
    Simple string-based template function. Replaces {key} in str with values from data (defaults to __.data). Does not auto-sanitize — use for trusted data or call __.safify() on values.
    let html = __.template('Hello {name}, you have {count} messages', {
  name: 'Alice',
  count: 5
})
// "Hello Alice, you have 5 messages"

    Cookies

    Simple cookie management for feature flags, preferences, and lightweight state.

    Extras
    __.writeCookie(name, value, days)
    Sets a cookie with optional expiration. Omit days for a session cookie. Sets path=/ by default.
    <button ps-click="__.writeCookie"
  writeCookie-name="theme" writeCookie-value="dark"
  writeCookie-days="365">Remember Theme</button>
    __.getCookie(name) → string|undefined
    Reads a cookie value by name. Returns undefined if the cookie doesn't exist.
    __.removeCookie(name)
    Deletes a cookie by setting its expiration to the past.
    __.succeedIfCookie(name, value) → Promise
    Resolves if the named cookie equals value. Useful as a chain gate: only continue if a cookie is set.
    <div startup="__.succeedIfCookie, showDashboard"
  succeedIfCookie-name="loggedIn" succeedIfCookie-value="true"
  succeedIfCookie-error="showLogin"></div>
    __.failIfCookie(name, value) → Promise
    Rejects if the named cookie equals value. The inverse of succeedIfCookie.

    Patterns & Recipes

    Copy-paste patterns for common UI components. Most require zero custom JavaScript.

    Tab Switching

    Tabs with active state

    <div class="tab-bar">
  <button ps-click="__.switchTo" class="btn active"
    switchTo-show="#panel-a" switchTo-hide=".panels"
    switchTo-siblings=".tab-bar .btn" debounce="0">Alpha</button>
  <button ps-click="__.switchTo" class="btn"
    switchTo-show="#panel-b" switchTo-hide=".panels"
    switchTo-siblings=".tab-bar .btn" debounce="0">Beta</button>
</div>
<div id="panel-a" class="panels">Alpha content</div>
<div id="panel-b" class="panels hidden">Beta content</div>

    Modal Open/Close

    Modal with backdrop dismiss

    <!-- Trigger -->
<button ps-click="__.show" show-selector="#modal">Open Modal</button>

<!-- Modal -->
<div class="modal-bg hidden" id="modal"
  ps-click="__.hide" hide-selector="#modal">
  <div class="modal-box" ps-click="__.noop" debounce="0">
    <h3>Confirm</h3>
    <p>Are you sure?</p>
    <button ps-click="__.hide"
      hide-selector="#modal" debounce="0">Cancel</button>
    <button ps-click="doAction, __.hide"
      hide-selector="#modal" debounce="0">Confirm</button>
  </div>
</div>

    __.noop on the inner box stops click propagation so clicking inside the modal does not trigger the backdrop's __.hide.

    Accordion

    togglePanel-selector="#a1">What is Popstart? ▼</button>

  <button ps-click="__.togglePanel"
    togglePanel-selector="#a2">Do I need a build step? ▼</button>
  <div class="hidden" id="a2">No. Just include the script.</div>
</div>

    Form Submit Chain

    Validate, scrape, post, show result

    <form ps-submit="__.validate, __.scrape, __.post, __.alertSuccess"
  post-url="/api/contact"
  alertSuccess-msg="Sent!"
  post-error="__.alertError">
  <input name="name" required placeholder="Name">
  <input name="email" type="email" required placeholder="Email">
  <textarea name="message" required placeholder="Message"></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Send Message</button>
</form>

    Chain: validate → scrape all inputs into __.data.form → POST as JSON → show success. If validation fails, chain stops. If POST fails, __.alertError shows the server error.

    Toggle Show/Hide

  toggle-selector="#details">Show Details</button>
<div class="hidden" id="details">
  Extra information here...

    Delete from List

    Self-removing list items

  <li>Item 1 <button ps-click="__.del"

  <li>Item 2 <button ps-click="__.del"

    Copy to Clipboard with Feedback

    Loading States

    Button loading during API call

  loading-selector="#save" loading-loadingtext="Saving..."
  post-url="/api/save"

  post-error="__.done, __.alertError"

</ul>
