    Configuration

    Customize event binding, debounce timing, attribute prefixes, and more via __.config.

    Setting Configuration

    Set __.config properties before loading Popstart, or modify them after. Popstart merges your values with defaults — you only need to set what you want to change.

    <script>
// Set before loading popstart
window.__ = { config: {
  DebounceTimes: { click: 100, input: 500 },
  sanitize: false
}}
</script>
<script src="popstart-core.js"></script>

    Or modify after loading:

    <script src="popstart-core.js"></script>
<script>
__.config.BoundEventNames.push('mouseover', 'focus')
__.config.DebounceTimes.click = 100
__.config.httpHeaders = { 'Authorization': 'Bearer token123' }
</script>

    All Options

    OptionDefaultDescription
    BoundEventNames ['mouseup','change','input','keyup','submit','click'] DOM events that Popstart listens for. Push additional event names to bind more.
    AttrPrefixes ['ps-','','data-','x-'] Attribute prefixes checked in order. First match wins. ps-click is checked before click.
    DebounceTimes {click:50, mouseup:50, input:300, change:300, keyup:300} Per-event debounce in milliseconds. Set to 0 to disable for an event type.
    StopPropagationEventNames ['submit','mouseup','change','click'] Events that get preventDefault() + stopPropagation() by default.
    AlwaysPreventDefault false When true, prevents default on all events, not just the ones in StopPropagationEventNames.
    AlwaysPreventClickPropagation true Controls click propagation behavior.
    DontAutostart false When true, Popstart does NOT auto-bind on DOMContentLoaded. Call __.Popstart() manually.
    sanitize true When true, __.populate() and __.populateEach() auto-escape data values via __.safify(). Set to false if you sanitize server-side.
    httpHeaders {} Default headers for all HTTP requests (e.g., auth tokens). Extras only.
    DetectDOMChildListChanges true MutationObserver watches for child element additions/removals and rebinds events.
    DetectDOMSubtreeChanges true MutationObserver watches for changes in the subtree.
    DetectDOMAttrChanges undefined Set to true to watch for attribute changes (can be noisy).
    DetectDOMAttrChangesFilter undefined Array of attribute names to watch (limits DetectDOMAttrChanges).

    Per-Element Overrides

    Some settings can be overridden per-element via attributes:

    AttributeEffect
    debounce="500"Override debounce time for this element
    debounce="0"Disable debounce for this element
    ps-click-prevent-default="false"Don't prevent default for this event on this element

    Advanced Topics

    Deep dives into the DOM watcher, data flow, custom function registration, and real-time streaming.

    DOMWatcher — Automatic Rebinding

    __.DOMWatcher uses a MutationObserver to watch for DOM changes. When new elements with event attributes are added (e.g., via AJAX, templating, or SPA navigation), Popstart automatically rebinds events. This means dynamically injected HTML just works.

    // DOMWatcher is started automatically after startup.
// Control it manually:
__.DOMWatcher.stop()   // pause observation
__.DOMWatcher.start()  // resume observation

// Check if running:
__.DOMWatcher.isRunning  // boolean

    The watcher is debounced at 500ms to avoid excessive rebinding during rapid DOM changes.

    How it works: When the observer fires, Popstart calls __.Popstart(), which resets all event bindings and re-scans the entire document. This is safe because __.Binding.resetAll() unbinds before rebinding, preventing duplicate handlers.

    Data Flow with writedatapath / readdatapath

    These attributes create a pipeline between functions in a chain:

    <div startup="__.get, __.populateEach"
  get-url="/api/users"
  get-writedatapath="users"
  populateEach-selector="#user-list"
  populateEach-readdatapath="users"></div>

    Flow:

    1. __.get fetches /api/users and stores the result in __.data.users (via writedatapath)
    2. __.populateEach reads from __.data.users (via readdatapath) and renders the list

    Without writedatapath, the result is stored at __.data["__.get"] (the function path). Using writedatapath gives you a clean, predictable key.

    Custom Function Registration

    Any function on window or on the __ object is callable from attributes. No registration step needed:

    <script>
// Option 1: Global function (window)
function saveUser(url, el) {
  return fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ name: el.querySelector('[name=name]').value })
  })
}

// Option 2: Namespaced on window
window.app = {
  save: function(url) { return fetch(url, { method: 'POST' }) },
  reload: function() { location.reload() }
}

// Option 3: On the __ object
__.myHelper = function(selector) {
  __.el(selector).forEach(el => el.classList.add('highlighted'))
}
</script>

<!-- All three are callable: -->
<button ps-click="saveUser" saveUser-url="/api/user">Save</button>
<button ps-click="app.save" save-url="/api/data">Save</button>
<button ps-click="__.myHelper" myHelper-selector=".items">Highlight</button>
    Important: Do NOT use <script type="module">. Module-scoped functions are invisible to Popstart because it looks for functions on window and __.

    SSE (Server-Sent Events)

    Open an SSE stream that auto-accumulates messages into __.data and optionally renders them:

    <ul id="feed">
  <template><li>{message} &mdash; <small>{timestamp}</small></li></template>
</ul>

<div startup="__.sseOpen"
  sseOpen-url="/api/events"
  sseOpen-writedatapath="feed"
  sseOpen-selector="#feed"></div>

<button ps-click="__.sseClose"
  sseClose-url="/api/events">Disconnect</button>

    Each SSE message is JSON-parsed and appended to __.data.feed as an array. If selector is set, __.populateEach is called automatically to re-render the list.

    WebSocket

    Same pattern as SSE, but bidirectional:

    <!-- Open WebSocket and render messages -->
<div startup="__.wsOpen"
  wsOpen-url="wss://example.com/ws"
  wsOpen-writedatapath="messages"
  wsOpen-selector="#chat"></div>

<!-- Send a message -->
<input id="msg-input" ps-keyup="sendOnEnter">
<script>
function sendOnEnter(ev, el) {
  if (ev.key === 'Enter') {
    __.wsSend('wss://example.com/ws', { text: el.value })
    el.value = ''
  }
}
</script>

<!-- Close -->
<button ps-click="__.wsClose"
  wsClose-url="wss://example.com/ws">Disconnect</button>

    Plugins

    When popstart-plugins.js is loaded, add ps-use="pluginName" to any element. Plugins are lazy-loaded from __.config.pluginRoot (default /popstart/plugins):

    <div ps-use="router"></div>
<div ps-use="dragdrop"></div>

    Router Plugin

    Client-side routing with URL parameters:

    <div ps-use="router"></div>

<a ps-click="__.navigate" navigate-url="/users">Users</a>

<div route="/users">User List</div>
<div route="/users/:id" routed="loadUser">User Detail</div>
<div route="*">404 - Not Found</div>

    Route parameters are extracted to __.data.route.params (e.g., __.data.route.params.id).

    Drag & Drop Plugin

    Sortable lists and file drop zones:

    <div ps-use="dragdrop"></div>

<!-- Sortable list -->
<ul sortable sorted="onReorder">
  <li>Item A</li>
  <li>Item B</li>
  <li>Item C</li>
</ul>

<!-- File drop zone -->
<div dropzone="handleFiles">Drop files here</div>

    Security Best Practices

    • Always use __.safify() when interpolating user data into HTML strings
    • Template functions (__.populate, __.populateEach) auto-sanitize when __.config.sanitize is true (default)
    • Raw HTML functions (__.html, __.append, etc.) do NOT auto-sanitize
    • Load DOMPurify for production-grade sanitization — Popstart auto-upgrades __.safify if DOMPurify is detected
    • Set __.config.sanitize = false only if you sanitize server-side before storage

    Lifecycle Summary

    DOMContentLoaded
  → __.Startup()
    → __.Popstart()          // scan DOM, bind all events
    → run startup functions  // startup, startup1, startup2
    → __.DOMWatcher.start()  // watch for future DOM changes
      → MutationObserver
        → __.Popstart()      // rebind on DOM change (debounced 500ms)

User Interaction (click, submit, etc.)
  → __.PopEvent()            // parse attribute, find functions
    → __.functionFinder()    // locate function on __ or window
    → __.getArgs()           // parse parameter names from source
    → __.GetStringAttr()     // read attribute values for each param
    → fn.apply(el, args)     // call function with element as this
    → store result           // __.data[path] and writedatapath
    → next function or error handler

    Details / Summary zero JS

    CSS only · native HTML5 disclosure with custom styling
    What is Popstart?
    Popstart is an HTML-driven JavaScript library that maps DOM events to function chains via HTML attributes. No build step required.
    How big is it?
    The core library is 12KB gzipped. The full build with all extras is ~18KB gzipped (~57KB unminified).
    Do I need a framework?
    No. Popstart works with vanilla HTML. Add a script tag and start writing attributes. It also plays well with any framework.
    Is it production-ready?
    Popstart is used in production on multiple sites. It has zero dependencies and handles edge cases gracefully.

  <details>
    <summary>How big is it?</summary>
    <div class="details-body">...</div>
  </details>
</div>

    Scroll Reveal

    IntersectionObserver · animate on scroll into view

    Scroll down inside the container to reveal items.

    First Section

    Fades in from below as you scroll.

    Second Section

    Each item animates independently.

    Third Section

    Uses IntersectionObserver for performance.

    Fourth Section

    No scroll event listeners needed.

    Fifth Section

    Smooth CSS transitions do the rest.

    Final Section

    You have reached the end.

    HTML
    <div class="sr-scroll">
  <div class="sr-item">
    <h4>Section</h4>
    <p>Content reveals on scroll.</p>
  </div>
  <!-- more items... -->
</div>
    JavaScript
    function initScrollReveal() {
  document.querySelectorAll('.sr-scroll')
    .forEach(function(scroller) {
      var obs = new IntersectionObserver(
        function(entries) {
          entries.forEach(function(entry) {
            if (entry.isIntersecting)
              entry.target.classList.add('sr-visible')
          })
        },
        { root: scroller, threshold: 0.2 }
      )
      scroller.querySelectorAll('.sr-item')
        .forEach(function(el) { obs.observe(el) })
    })
}
// called on page load
initScrollReveal()

    Sticky Header zero JS

    CSS only · position:sticky in scrollable container
    Project Overview

    This section demonstrates how position:sticky works within a scrollable overflow container. The header above stays pinned to the top as you scroll through content.

    Sticky positioning is a hybrid of relative and fixed positioning. The element is treated as relative until it crosses a specified threshold, then it becomes fixed.

    Technical Details

    The key requirement is that the parent container must have a defined height and overflow-y set to auto or scroll. Without this, sticky has nothing to stick within.

    Combine with backdrop-filter for a modern glass effect that lets content scroll beneath the header while remaining readable.

    Best Practices

    Use sticky headers for long scrollable sections where context is important. Table headers, sidebar navigation, and section labels are ideal use cases.

    Always test in containers with overflow:hidden on ancestors, as this can break sticky behavior unexpectedly.

    For mobile, ensure the sticky element does not take up too much vertical space, as screen real estate is limited.

    HTML
    <div class="sh-scroll"
  style="max-height:200px;overflow-y:auto">
  <div class="sh-header"
    style="position:sticky;top:0;
    backdrop-filter:blur(12px)">
    Section Title
  </div>
  <div class="sh-section">
    <p>Content...</p>
  </div>
  <!-- more sections... -->
</div>
    CSS
    .sh-scroll {
  max-height: 200px;
  overflow-y: auto;
}
.sh-header {
  position: sticky; top: 0;
  background: var(--glass);
  backdrop-filter: blur(12px);
  z-index: 2;
}
    JavaScript
    // zero custom JavaScript needed

    .px-container {
  height: 200px;

}
.px-layer {
  min-height: 120px;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  background-attachment: fixed;
}
.px-bg1 {
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1a1a3e, #0f3460);
}
.px-bg2 {
  background: linear-gradient(135deg,
    var(--accent), var(--accent2));
  background-attachment: local;
}

    .hl-yellow { background:linear-gradient(
  180deg, transparent 55%, rgba(232,184,74,0.35) 55%) }

  90deg, var(--accent-glow), rgba(90,173,221,0.2));
  border-radius:3px }
.hl-box { border:1px solid var(--accent);
  border-radius:3px; color:var(--accent) }

.hl-glow { text-shadow:0 0 8px var(--accent-glow) }

    Split Pane

    onmousedown · resizable vertical split with draggable divider
    Editor

    This is the left pane. Drag the divider to resize. Content reflows automatically as the pane width changes.

    Useful for code editors, file managers, or any side-by-side comparison layout.

    Preview

    This is the right pane. It grows and shrinks inversely with the left pane.

    The divider handle shows a visual indicator and highlights on hover.

    HTML
    <div class="spp-container">
  <div class="spp-left">Left pane</div>
  <div class="spp-divider"
    onmousedown="sppDrag(event)"
    ontouchstart="sppDrag(event)"></div>
  <div class="spp-right">Right pane</div>
</div>
    JavaScript
    function sppDrag(ev) {
  ev.preventDefault()
  var divider = ev.currentTarget ||
    ev.target.closest('.spp-divider')
  var container = divider.closest('.spp-container')
  var left = container.querySelector('.spp-left')
  var right = container.querySelector('.spp-right')
  function move(e) {
    var rect = container.getBoundingClientRect()
    var x = (e.touches ? e.touches[0].clientX : e.clientX)
    var pct = Math.max(15, Math.min(85,
      ((x - rect.left) / rect.width) * 100))
    left.style.flex = '0 0 ' + pct + '%'
    right.style.flex = '0 0 ' + (100 - pct - 2) + '%'
  }
  function up() {
    document.removeEventListener('mousemove', move)
    document.removeEventListener('mouseup', up)
    document.removeEventListener('touchmove', move)
    document.removeEventListener('touchend', up)
  }
  document.addEventListener('mousemove', move)
  document.addEventListener('mouseup', up)
  document.addEventListener('touchmove', move)
  document.addEventListener('touchend', up)
}

    Print View zero JS

    __.toggleClass · toggle print-friendly styling on content

    Project Status Report

    This document demonstrates how content can be toggled between a rich themed view and a print-friendly layout with a single attribute.

    Key Finding: The HTML-driven approach reduced JavaScript by 94% compared to the React prototype.

    Current sprint velocity is trending upward. The team completed 42 story points this iteration.

    Q1 2026
    HTML
    <button ps-click="__.toggleClass"
  toggleClass-selector="#pv-content"
  toggleClass-classes="print-mode">
  🖨 Toggle Print View
</button>

<div class="pv-content" id="pv-content">
  <h4>Project Status Report</h4>
  <p>Content here...</p>
  <span class="pv-badge">Q1 2026</span>
</div>
    CSS
    .pv-content {
  background: var(--bg2); color: var(--fg);
  transition: all 0.3s ease;
}
.pv-content.print-mode {
  background: #fff !important;
  color: #111 !important;
}
.pv-content.print-mode .pv-badge {
  background: #555 !important;
}
